haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts attempt 1 at 02:00 UTC daily. It extracts rows with lower < updated_at <= cutoff from the replica, lower being HWM minus 2h, including soft-deleted rows.
haiku-low.q2: A bulk-import transaction can stay open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped at write time, so its rows become visible up to 90 minutes late.
haiku-low.q3: The edit changes updated_at, so a later nightly lookback picks it up. The merge updates the row when src.updated_at >= tgt.updated_at.
haiku-low.q4: Soft delete sets deleted_at, a write that changes updated_at. The merge sets is_deleted = true in place on wh.orders. The row is never removed.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt is marked failed, and the HWM and wh.orders stay unchanged. The scheduler waits 15 minutes and retries, up to 3 attempts. After the third failure it pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the previous committed state. #data-alerts gets a staleness alert from the 06:00 watchdog. On-call is paged only after the third attempt fails.
haiku-low.q7: Sunday's reconciliation. It compares count and checksum per creation day over the last 30 days, then reloads any mismatched day from the replica into wh.orders.
haiku-low.q8: The merge keeps only the latest updated_at per order_id and updates only if src.updated_at >= tgt.updated_at. Identical re-merges change nothing.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in etl.control.high_water_mark for pipeline orders. It is set to the attempt's cutoff, only if larger, inside the merge transaction at commit.
haiku-low.q10: wh.orders changes only inside the single merge transaction, so a 06:00 dashboard refresh sees the whole night or none of it.
haiku-low.q11: The retry first deletes all etl.stg_orders rows, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. It reuses the same HWM, so it extracts HWM minus 2h up to a fresh cutoff.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads every row created on each mismatched day from the replica. One transaction merges them with the same rule. The HWM is not touched.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts attempt 1 at 02:00 UTC daily. It extracts rows from the replica's orders table where HWM - 2h < updated_at <= cutoff, including soft-deleted rows.
sonnet.q2: A bulk import is an app transaction that can stay open up to 90 minutes. updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit time, so rows become visible up to 90 minutes after their updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit changes updated_at, so a later nightly extract picks it up (window lower < updated_at <= cutoff). It is staged and merged into wh.orders, updating the row if src.updated_at >= tgt.updated_at.
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at, which is a write that changes updated_at. The extract picks it up and the merge updates the row in place with is_deleted = true. The row is never removed.
sonnet.q5: The run is marked failed (by the job, or by the scheduler if the job cannot). HWM and wh.orders are unchanged. The scheduler waits 15 minutes and starts the next attempt, up to 3 attempts. After the third failure it pages on-call and reconciliation does not run.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the previous committed state. The watchdog at 06:00 finds no nightly success row for today's run_date and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts. On-call is paged only if the third attempt failed.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares count and checksum per creation day over the last 30 days against the replica, reloads mismatched days from the replica, and merges them into wh.orders.
sonnet.q8: The merge query dedups staging to the highest updated_at per order_id. It updates a matching row only when src.updated_at >= tgt.updated_at, so older versions never overwrite newer ones. Re-merging an identical version changes nothing.
sonnet.q9: It is stored in etl.control (high_water_mark column) in the warehouse, and nowhere else. It is set to the attempt's cutoff, only if the cutoff is larger than the current value. This happens inside the single merge transaction, which commits together with the merge, the success mark and the staging cleanup.
sonnet.q10: wh.orders is the only table dashboards read, and it changes only inside the single merge transaction. A refresh sees the whole night or none of it. Staging is never read by dashboards.
sonnet.q11: The next attempt empties staging at its start (it deletes all rows in etl.stg_orders), so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. The retry reads the same unchanged HWM, so the lower bound is again HWM - 2h. It takes a fresh cutoff from the replica.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads all rows created on each mismatched day from the replica into staging, including soft-deleted rows. All mismatched days are applied in one transaction using the same merge rule (update if src.updated_at >= tgt.updated_at, insert if new), and the run's staging rows are deleted. It does not touch the HWM.
